new.name: Kurodyne
new.description: Kurodyne is a marketplace of skills, prompts, automation workflows, software tools, spreadsheets and templates that AI agents can search. Its Catalog MCP server is free to use with no account, so agents can search products, read reviews and pull each product's README. Sellers use a separate Seller Console MCP to have their own agent publish products and answer buyers. Prices run from $5 to $500, with a 20% fee per sale and no listing or monthly fees. A person reviews every listing, and packages are malware-scanned and fingerprinted.
new.pricing_detail: Free to browse and to search through the Catalog MCP. Products are priced by sellers from $5 to $500 in whole US dollars. Sellers pay no listing or monthly fee and a 20% platform fee per sale, plus Stripe processing; the first sellers to publish pay no platform fee for 3 months, according to its selling page, checked 27 Nov 2026.

new.name: Sandscale
new.description: Sandscale runs Firecracker microVM sandboxes, workspaces and build machines for AI agents. The pricing page on 27 Nov 2026 listed a free plan at $0 a month with 100 awake vCPU-hours, 3 concurrent sandboxes, 5 GB of storage and one workspace. Pro was $20 a month billed annually or $25 billed monthly, with 1,500 awake vCPU-hours. Team was $40 per member a month annually or $48 monthly, with 2,000 awake vCPU-hours per member. Usage past the hours was $0.05 per awake vCPU-hour, hour packs were $10 per 500 hours, and storage past the allowance was $0.15 per GB-month. The first 10 GB of storage was free. The docs tell Claude Code to connect to https://mcp.sandscale.dev/mcp. A POST initialize without a session on 27 Nov 2026 returned HTTP 401 and asked the caller to sign in.
new.pricing_detail: Free $0/mo: 100 awake vCPU-hours, 3 concurrent, 5 GB. Pro $20/mo annual or $25 monthly (1,500 vCPU-hours). Team $40/member/mo annual or $48 monthly. Overage $0.05 per awake vCPU-hour. Storage past the allowance $0.15/GB-month (sandscale.dev/pricing, 27 Nov 2026).

new.name: Provider Trust
new.description: Provider Trust is Script Master Labs' check of who is behind a site, API or data source before an agent quotes it or calls it. The product page on 27 Nov 2026 says it looks at provider identity, source ownership and observable trust signals, and that a reachable domain or a valid TLS certificate is not itself an endorsement. The page did not list a dollar price. A GET and a POST initialize to https://provider-trust-mcp.onrender.com/mcp both returned HTTP 200 and named the server provider-trust, version 1.2.0. This listing is only Provider Trust. It is not Agent Verify, Garage402 or Authority Engine.
new.pricing_detail: No dollar price on the product page on 27 Nov 2026. MCP initialize returned provider-trust v1.2.0.

new.name: Aethon AI
new.description: Aethon AI is a generative-engine-optimization product from Moment Intelligence. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 says it finds the life moments when people ask ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity for help, then works to get a brand recommended in those answers. Plans are Starter at $199 a month (50 moments, one industry, up to 10 seats), Pro at $399 (250 moments) and Business at $799 (600 moments, team workflows). Annual billing is shown as 20% less. A free Moment Check is offered before a paid plan. The page did not describe a permanent free product tier.
new.pricing_detail: Starter $199/mo (50 moments, up to 10 seats), Pro $399/mo (250 moments), Business $799/mo (600 moments). Annual billing saves 20% (aiaethon.com, 26 Nov 2026).

new.name: PopFestive
new.description: PopFestive turns one portrait into a Christmas profile picture or a short festive video. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 offered styles such as a Santa hat, anime, a 3D cartoon, a Nice List certificate, a pet portrait and a baby-on-a-reindeer clip. It asks for one clear photo of a face you have permission to use. Credits pay for downloads without a watermark. Basic is $29.90 a month for 100 credits, Pro is $49.90 for 300, and Family is $99.90 for 800. A 10-credit pack is $7.99 and a 50-credit pack is $29. The page says failed renders are free and that monthly credits refresh. This is a holiday photo effect, not a face-swap product.
new.pricing_detail: Basic $29.90/mo (100 credits), Pro $49.90/mo (300), Family $99.90/mo (800). Packs: 10 credits $7.99, 50 credits $29. Failed renders free (popfestive.com, 26 Nov 2026).

new.name: HIVE402
new.description: HIVE402 is Script Master Labs' live directory of x402 endpoints that agents can pay. The homepage on 26 Nov 2026 showed 67,157 paid endpoints, 43,879 of them marked verified payable, 2,187 operators and 6 payment rails, and it said those figures are re-checked from settlement records. A GET to https://hive402.scriptmasterlabs.com/mcp returned HTTP 200 and named the server x402-agent-idea-forge, with tools such as search_catalog and get_listing. The page describes a free Rescue check that reads an endpoint's catalog state, and a 0.005 USDC OMNIGATE fee leg on some paid flows. This listing is only HIVE402. It is not SqueezeOS, Token Verdict, Verdict Protocol or Authority Engine.
new.pricing_detail: Homepage on 26 Nov 2026: a live paid-endpoint market. Rescue checks are described as free. A 0.005 USDC OMNIGATE fee leg is named on some paid flows. No monthly subscription price was on that page.

new.name: Wavegrain
new.description: Wavegrain makes curated TikTok slideshows and Instagram carousels and can schedule them from an assistant. The hosted MCP at https://wavegrain.com/api/mcp uses OAuth for Claude and ChatGPT and an access key for other clients. On 24 Nov 2026 the pricing page listed Starter at $29 a month (300 credits, about 100 slideshows, 5 brands), Pro at $49 a month (800 credits, 15 brands) and Agency at $99 a month (2,000 credits). The page said posts go to TikTok and YouTube today, with Instagram, Facebook, Threads and LinkedIn still coming. Yearly billing was listed as two months free.
new.pricing_detail: Starter $29/mo (300 credits), Pro $49/mo (800 credits), Agency $99/mo (2,000 credits). Yearly billing listed as two months free (wavegrain.com/pricing, 24 Nov 2026).

new.name: aichat.md
new.description: aichat.md is an AI assistant that answers customer messages on a website and on chat channels such as Instagram and WhatsApp, with setup the maker says takes 24 to 48 hours. On 24 Nov 2026 the English page listed Starter at $49 a month (2,000 credits, about 2,000 conversations, one assistant, Instagram, WhatsApp and the website), Pro at $150 a month (10,000 credits, two assistants, connections such as Altegio, Syrve, AmoCRM, Bitrix24 and Google Sheets, plus handover to a person) and Scale at $490 a month (50,000 credits, separate assistants per department). Plans are monthly and can be cancelled.
new.pricing_detail: Starter $49/mo (2,000 credits), Pro $150/mo (10,000 credits), Scale $490/mo (50,000 credits). Monthly, cancel any time (aichat.md/en, 24 Nov 2026).

stars.name: REA
stars.description: MCP server and CLI that lets coding agents reverse engineer native binaries, Electron and JavaScript apps, .NET assemblies and live websites, using Ghidra, Hopper or IDA under the hood.

stars.name: OpenClaw
stars.description: OpenClaw is an MIT-licensed personal AI assistant that runs on your own computer and answers in the chat apps you already use, including Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram and WhatsApp, with native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows and Linux. State, memory and credentials stay on your hardware, models and harnesses such as Claude, Codex or local models are swappable plugins, and one gateway can run a personal or shared multiplayer assistant. It is stewarded by the non-profit OpenClaw Foundation with no paid tier or hosted service.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); you pay only for the model providers you connect.

stars.name: ECC
stars.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond

stars.name: DeepSeek Harness
stars.description: DeepSeek's open-source agent harness with a local web UI, built so that every tool, model and scheduled task is a swappable plugin; still a developer preview.

stars.name: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
stars.description: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's MIT-licensed, self-improving agent with a built-in learning loop: it writes skills from completed tasks, refines them in use, keeps agent-curated memory and searches its own past conversations. It runs on anything from a $5 VPS to serverless infrastructure, offers a full terminal UI, and one gateway serves Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and the CLI, with any model via Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI or your own endpoint.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); model usage billed by your chosen provider.

stars.name: opencode
stars.description: OpenCode is an MIT-licensed open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, with a beta desktop app, that works with many model providers instead of locking you to one. Install it with a one-line script, npm, Homebrew, pacman, mise or Nix, then let it read your repository, edit files and run commands from a keyboard-driven TUI.
stars.pricing_detail: Free and open source (MIT); bring your own model provider.

stars.name: n8n
stars.description: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes; self-host or cloud.

stars.name: Firecrawl
stars.description: Firecrawl is an AGPL-3.0 web data API for AI agents, open source and available as a hosted service: Search returns full page content for web results, Scrape turns any URL into clean Markdown, HTML, screenshots or structured JSON, Crawl and Map cover whole sites, Interact clicks, scrolls and types before extracting, and Parse converts PDFs and DOCX files. It handles proxies, rate limits and JavaScript-heavy pages for you, and connects to any agent or MCP client with a single command.
